text:
maria: heads up — onboarding a quantized judge model into eval-runner failed CI on the new consistency check. stack trace attached.

alan: ugh, which job?

maria: eval-runner-quant-job on main, job id `job/2026-03-19-qlt-77`. failing assertion is in judge_consistency.py: `assert agreement_rate >= 0.7`

tess: can you paste the failing logs?

maria: ```
E 03/19 14:12:02 runner: loaded model redwood/judge-xxl-8bit-q4 -> OK
E 03/19 14:12:07 eval: anchor set mismatch: expected 50 anchors, found 37
E 03/19 14:12:07 eval: disagreement_rate=0.38, agreement_rate=0.62 < 0.7
E 03/19 14:12:07 metrics: raise AssertionError('consistency check failed')
```

sam: 37 anchors?? that's suspicious. did quant drop some tokens during preprocessing?

jing: our anchor sampling code changed in the last PR — we switched to dedupe by string before truncation to avoid near-duplicates. could reduce anchor count for some datasets.

alan: dedupe before truncation can collapse paraphrases into same string, so anchor size can shrink. but agreement drop to .62 suggests more than just fewer anchors.

maria: I re-ran locally with full float model and got agreement_rate=0.78 on same anchor set (the float model used by the old runner). quant model is lower.

tess: is the quantized judge being loaded with the same decoding params? temperature/penalty mismatch can flip decisions.

maria: loading code uses `model_config_overrides={'temperature':0.0}` in both cases. logits scaling? the quant runtime applies per-layer scale table at runtime.

ci-bot: :warning: job eval-runner-quant-job failed — see https://ci.internal/jobs/job/2026-03-19-qlt-77/logs

sam: two hypotheses: 1) quant noise reduces deterministic tie resolution (more ties, different tie-break picks), 2) rounding changed numeric comparators used by judge ensemble scoring.

jing: we have a gating check that treats exact string matches specially in the judge rubric. quantization could be altering whitespace/utf8 normalization if tokenization differs.

maria: good point — I diffed token ids for the anchor prompts between float and quant configs. some token ids differ around special chars (em-dash, nonbreaking space).

alan: then maybe the dedupe-before-truncation combined with tokenization differences is making anchors inconsistent between float and quant runs. that could explain both anchor count and agreement delta.

tess: actionable? revert dedupe order for the job or canonicalize unicode before dedupe/tokenize. also bump the consistency threshold for new models during onboarding to 0.6 for quant variants so we can iterate without blocking main CI.

maria: propose small plan: 1) patch eval harness to normalize unicode NFKC before dedupe/truncation 2) add a token-level canonicalization step for judge anchor creation 3) temporary CI config override for quant models to use agreement_rate >= 0.6 and flag as "needs review" 4) run targeted ablation comparing float vs quant on fixed anchor set to isolate rounding vs anchor-selection effects.

sam: +1 to plan. I'd also like to add a debug mode that emits sample judge outputs and token ids for a few anchors — won't log sensitive data but will help diagnose.

jing: I'll file a tiny PR to do NFKC normalization and instrument anchor sampling.

ops-bot: scheduled run created: `run/2026-03-19-qlt-debug-1` — will execute float vs quant ablation across 200 anchors. ETA ~ 30m.

maria: thanks. one more ask: can we add a tie-breaker fallback that uses soft-score mean over top-k instead of strict argmax for judges, to reduce sensitivity to tiny logit shifts?

alan: that changes evaluation semantics though. we should gate that behind a feature flag and only apply it for onboarding/quant runs.

tess: agree. make it opt-in per-job and mark outputs in dashboard as "soft-argmax" so reviewers know which runs used fallback.

maria: noted. I'll update the job config and the onboarding checklist: "if quant model fails consistency, enable soft-argmax + unicode normalization and re-run ablation"

sam: after the ablation, if the float vs quant disagreement is concentrated on edge cases we can add targeted anchor examples to the eval set to improve robustness.

jing: PR opened: https://git.internal/p/eng-ml/patches/2345 — includes NFKC normalization + extra logging.

maria: great, running ops-bot job now. will update when it finishes. :memo:
